title: The impacts and incentives inherent in destination-based carbon pricing: An Indian Case study
description: Analysis of destination-based carbon pricing mechanisms and their effects on industrial behaviour, competitiveness, public revenue, and emissions.
methodology: Partial equilibrium modelling of carbon price pass-through; sectoral competitiveness assessment.
assumptions: Carbon price is enforced at point of consumption/destination
Trade-exposed sectors can relocate or pass costs to consumers
Revenue is recycled into public programmes
limitations: India-specific industrial structure; border adjustment debates ongoing globally
Informal economy responses not fully modelled

sources.title: UNFCCC KCI — India destination-based carbon pricing

nodes.label: Firms shift to cleaner inputs & efficiency
Production mix moves to lower-carbon processes

outcomes.description: Price signal reduces emissions in covered sectors
Carbon fee revenue available for climate and social programmes
Export-oriented industries face cost pressures; may shift supply chains
Job losses in carbon-intensive industries offset by growth in clean sectors

trade_offs.negative_effect: Higher consumer prices for energy-intensive goods
Risk of carbon leakage to jurisdictions without pricing
